newsitem.title: FINLAND: AMER SAYS BRITON AGREES TO BUY K-STAKE.
newsitem.headline: AMER SAYS BRITON AGREES TO BUY K-STAKE.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy said on Monday its vote-strong K-shareholders had offered to sell a majority of their holdings to a Briton, Jonathan Bryan Guinness, third Lord Moyne.
"Lord Moyne has accepted the offer subject to the fulfilment of certain conditions specified in the bid," the company said in a statement.
If the deal is formally approved, it said, "the voting majority of the Amer Group ... would pass to Lord Moyne, who would hold a voting power of 58.4 percent."

Heikki Kauppi, a representative of Amer's four K-shareholders at an extraordinary meeting, told reporters the news meant holders of K-series shares "are unlikely to approve" a planned conversion of unlisted K-shares to A stock.

That had been planned after Amer's four main owners, all Finnish institutions, about a year ago failed to reach agreement on the sale of their stock. Conversion would enable the stock to be freely traded on the bourse.
As a first stage, Lord Moyne would acquire 1.1 million K shares for 301 million markka. After the completion of the planned transaction, he would hold 4.6 percent of shares and 58.4 percent of votes.
The current K-shareholders, who now control 90.5 percent of votes in the company, would retain 6.9 percent of shares and 3.0 percent of votes while other A-shareholders would have the rest.
A news conference will be held at 1530 local time/1230 GMT.
At the Helsinki stock exchange, a spokewoman said it was not yet clear when trade in Amer's shares would resume. Trade in the shares was suspended before the opening.
